title: Cabinet Air Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Cabinet temperature sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: Delfield commercial reach-ins, prep tables, and undercounters use a cabinet air thermistor. E1 indicates the sensor is open, shorted, or out of range. Without it the controller defaults to safe operation but cannot regulate temperature accurately.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM thermistor and route harness clear of moving parts.

whenToCallPro: If new sensor fails, controller needs service.

faq.a: Yes; resistance curves vary by part number.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E2 indicates the evaporator coil thermistor used for defrost termination is open or shorted. Defrost cycles will run for max time instead of terminating on temperature, which can damage food and waste energy.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for pinched or damaged wiring at evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM evap thermistor with thermal contact to coil.

whenToCallPro: If sensor good, controller needs evaluation.

faq.a: Sensor must contact coil for accurate temp; loose mounting gives false readings.

title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: Evap fan stalled or feedback missing.
fullDescription: Without evaporator airflow, cabinet cannot maintain temperature and the coil ices up. E3 fires when the evap fan motor fails. Causes are seized bearings, ice impingement, or failed motor.

fixSteps.title: Defrost manually
fixSteps.instruction: Empty cabinet and run manual defrost or power off until thawed.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: Spin blade by hand; verify free rotation. Test motor with multimeter.

whenToCallPro: Persistent icing without obvious cause needs refrigeration tech.

faq.a: Failed defrost or excess infiltration; both prevent normal air flow.

title: High Temperature Alarm
fullDescription: E4 / HI alarm fires when cabinet temperature is above the safe range for an extended time. Causes include door left open, refrigeration failure, dirty condenser.

causes.cause: Door left open or gasket failure

fixSteps.title: Verify door/gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm door closes and gasket seals fully.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant work requires EPA certification.

faq.a: Address food safety immediately; track temperatures.

title: Low Temperature Alarm
fullDescription: E5/LO indicates cabinet ran below safe range. Causes include controller miscalibration, stuck contactor, or sensor errors.

fixSteps.title: Test contactor
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm contactor opens with thermostat satisfied.

whenToCallPro: Refrigeration controls beyond setpoint need tech.

faq.a: Often a sensor reading high so compressor over-cools.

title: Defrost Timeout
shortDescription: Defrost cycle exceeded max time without termination.
fullDescription: E6 fires when the defrost cycle runs to maximum without the evap thermistor reaching termination temperature. Often the thermistor is misreading, the heater failed, or icing is severe.

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Empty cabinet and let evaporator fully thaw.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance of defrost heater; replace if open.

whenToCallPro: If heater good, refrigeration cycle issue likely; needs tech.

faq.a: Default 4-6 cycles per day; adjustable in controller.

title: Compressor Lockout
fullDescription: E7 indicates the compressor was locked out due to repeated faults: short cycling, overload, or loss of protection signal. Cycling power without fixing the cause leads to repeat failure.

fixSteps.title: Tech diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Refrigeration tech to test compressor and refrigerant system.

whenToCallPro: Compressor and refrigerant work requires certified service.

faq.a: Only after diagnosis; repeats damage compressor.

title: Door Open Alarm
shortDescription: Door left open beyond timer threshold.
fullDescription: E8 alarms when a door has been open longer than the controller threshold. Helps prevent product loss. Causes include door not latching, gasket failure, or heavy traffic.

fixSteps.title: Inspect door/gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Replace torn gasket; adjust hinges so door self-closes.

whenToCallPro: Hinge/door reframe rarely needs tech.

faq.a: Often 60-180 seconds, configurable in controller menu.

title: Condensate Pan Overflow
fullDescription: Some Delfield prep tables monitor the condensate pan. E9 fires when level rises beyond safe, indicating clogged drain or evaporator pan heater failure.

fixSteps.title: Clear drain
fixSteps.instruction: Flush condensate line with warm water and brush.

whenToCallPro: If pan heater failed, tech replacement needed.

faq.a: Flush drain quarterly to prevent blockage.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Display lost link with refrigeration controller.
fullDescription: E10 indicates communication breakdown between the user interface and main controller. Loose harness, moisture, or board failure are typical causes.
whenToCallPro: Board replacement requires service.

faq.a: Yes, helps preserve commercial controls.

title: High Cabinet Temperature
shortDescription: Cabinet temperature exceeded high alarm setpoint.
fullDescription: Delfield E21 alerts when cabinet temperature exceeds the high alarm threshold for longer than the configured delay. Often follows door left open or condenser problem.
symptoms: Possible food safety risk if ignored

fixSteps.title: Inspect and resolve obvious cause
fixSteps.instruction: Close doors, clean condenser, verify fans run.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor and switches
fixSteps.instruction: Test door switch and thermistors per service manual.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM Delfield replacement, verify, clear alarm.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant or sealed-system issues require EPA-certified service.

faq.q: Will Delfield log this code permanently?
faq.a: Yes, the controller stores the most recent alarms; clear them after service through the diagnostic menu.
